For Bunker -- quite contrary to Argent Adept -- the important thing is to get away from trying to do everything. He has a lot of options, but if you try and do ALL of them, you probably won't be ABLE to (unless you get lucky, or plan really well). While sitting and charging an Omni-Cannon can be really tempting, the constant chip damage you can get from a Flak Cannon, Grenade Launcher, and/or Gatling Gun really adds up over time. Also, don't underestimate Recharge Mode. It allows you to draw 3 CARDS A TURN, while also giving you an extra DR, allowing you to soak up lots of damage. Use it in conjunction with Omni-cannon and/or Gatling Gun to avoid being completely inactive, and then you can just pop out of it when you have lots of cards in your hand, then go Upgrade to get them all out and Turret to start blowing everything up.

 

Also, the Aux. Power Units are VERY HELPFUL. Use them often, and don't be afraid to use their draw 3 power. You can always use Recommissioned Hardware to get them back, if need be.

posts.name: Edwin
posts.cooked:
We've got a sexy new crop of heroes to play ("we" being the non-playtester non-preorderers of the general public, who had to wait for Vengeance to be generally available), so I think some of these old "what hero do you X" threads deserve bumping.  Today I got to try out a Vengeance hero for the first time, and I picked Parse (the other player took Naturalist, and we each also had an earlier hero, Ra for him and Omnitron-X for me).  I have to say, I was not impressed.

Granted, it's partially my own fault.  We were playing against Ambuscade who's historically been very pathetic, and I didn't want to faceroll him completely, so when Toxic Seaweed came out on the first round, I discarded Parse's hand, having not played a couple of cards that let you mess with the villain deck.  (I did first play Buffer Overflow, which lets you cancel a villain card play and force them to play a different card in its place.)  So between having skipped playing some of my more applicable cards and having discarded four of them, I was perhaps not getting the full Parse experience.  But I did read the cards even if I didn't play them, and so unless they prove a lot more effective in practice than they appeared to be initially, I find that they don't seem that great.  Lots of things require you to discard cards, and not much lets you draw them (there is one rather decent Power card that lets you draw every turn, but it requires you to not be shooting arrows at things).

The big issue I had with Parse is that she seems to be a lot like Mr. Fixer in a way - most of her cards are "magic bullets" which exist only to solve particular problems, but not all such problems are covered, and if you draw the wrong such card for the situation it's likely rather useless.  Parse is pretty good at dealing irreducible damage...but not all villains use heavy DR.  She can mess with the villain deck, but that isn't always incredibly helpful, though certainly it can decide a few games all by itself.  She has several ways of destroying Ongoings or Environment cards, but again, not everyg ame has Ongoing cards and the Environment isn't always a problem.  What she doesn't have very much of, other than her base power, is effects that are always useful; the raw effectiveness you get from heroes like Tempest and Bunker, who may not specialize in much but can pretty much always contribute somehow, seems likely to be a more sporadic experience with Parse.  If what the heroes need is for THAT TO DIE RIGHT NOW, about the best she's often able to do is plink for 2; she has the potential to offer some nice boosts, but they can be hard to string together, and it seems like very often she will want to spend her turn drawing 2 in order to have more options - while a hero like Wraith or Chrono-Ranger can have lots of options and still play every turn.

I dunno, I didn't hate her, I wasn't really even frustrated per se, but I definitely wasn't blown away.  (I ended up liking the Naturalist a lot more, even from across the table, and am very eager to play him myself.)  I wonder how long it's going to be before a "Fix Parse!" thread turns up.  Maybe my experience was atypical?  I'm not saying she's bad in the abstract, but I feel like she has a lot of potential to disappoint players, just as Fixer often can, even if they're both occasionally amazing.

Greywind:

Cards that allow draws:Buffer Overflow when used/destroyed (2 copies)Gauge when used (2 copies)Impossible Shot (3 copies)Quick Calculation choice 2 of 3 cards into hand (3 copies)Recompile; requires discarding but capable of drawing 6 cards (3 copies)

So you have 13 cards out of 40 that allow draws.

Just drawing one card off Impossible Shot or Buffer Overflow doesn't count for all that much.  By my count she has 8 cards which allow significant drawing, and only 5 that can produce a "card advantage" of more than +1, and one of those costs your Powers to do it while the other requires already having a decent-sized hand.  Recompile is good if you can manage it, so is Gauge, and Quick Calc is always nice if you have no other use for your play.  But a fifth to an eighth of the deck, while not awful, is certainly not an incredible amount when the hero's ability revolves so much around it.  Comparing her to Visionary and the Wraith, the former of which is the queen of drawing cards and sifting through situational ones to find what she needs, and the latter needs a card to deal damage but can almost guarantee finding such cards with Impromptu and Trust Fund, Parse doesn't seem to be great at this.  But I admit this is all based on one not-quite-average game, so I may well come to a different conclusion later.

The other thing I've got against Parse is that she has to have the absolute most useless incapacitated side of any hero.  Nearly every hero can either grant the survivors a card play or a power, and so those players are still able to make about half as much of the contribution to the game as if they were alive…what does Parse do?  I don't remember what her middle ability was, but I don't think it was impressive, and the other two are "peek at the villain's next card, but don't DO anything about it" and "draw a card".  That last one is pretty much the only choice in most situations, and it's not an immense help most of the time (certainly there are exceptions).  I know I won't plan on taking many chances the next time I play Parse; she makes me want to not die more than any other hero, because once she goes down she might practically just as well have been RFG'ed.  (I will have to play her in the Final Wasteland for exactly this reason, of course; it'll be a nice twist.)

Sefirit:

Is it just me or does Buffer Overflow completely shut down the worst card in any villain deck?

Buffer Overflow definitely has the potential to save your bacon; unfortunately, it was the first card I played in this game, and I completely squandered it.  Ambuscade played Armed and Dangerous, so I went to see what Device he'd pull out.  When it turned out to be the damn Cloak, I Buffered that - which unfortunately meant that he got an extra villain play from Buffer and one from Armed and Dangerous.  One of which was like a three-card chain, and the other was Vanish, so he got the Cloak anyway.  I just gave him an extra play to no profit.  Between that and the fact that he managed to NEVER ONCE pull a Trap, in ten turns and with 3 bonus card plays from Atlantis, it was by far the meanest Ambuscade game I've ever played.  The game ended with four other heroes dead and Ra alive at 1 HP after burning through either 3 or all 4 of his Staves, and that was after Naturalist did a good bit of healing and damage reduction.  It was ridiculous, and entirely my own fault; seeing the villain deck control in Parse's opening hand, I didn't want to use it, because Ambuscade can be pretty dull if you can stop his critical cards from coming.  So I basically let him just about faceroll us so that I wouldn't be facerolling him.  (Even so, he didn't quite manage to make this win either, which means he's the only villain who I've beaten every time I played him.)

For me, Parse is all about Updated Intel and Critical Multiplier.

 

Updated Intel (Whenever a villain card is played, look at the bottom card of a deck and put it on top or bottom) gives you so much huge control to the game board. Especially against multiple plays of villain cards. Sure you can neuter the villain and keep him from putting out anything crazy, by cycling up from the bottom, but more importantly is the ability to do the same to the heroes and stack the next card draw.

 

And Critical Multiplier, not being limited, becomes insane given the fact that half her cards require a discard to do anything. 

 

 

I wouldn't say there is a hero I 'get least' - I understand the concept and strategy of pretty much all of them.

 

I dislike playing visionary - she feels so reactive and while occasionally her powers can have a great affect most of the time I feel like its 'choosing between bad and worse' and a lot of sitting around doing only one thing.

Parse feels so much more interactive to me than visionary. I feel like I'm at least doing something (even if it has little actual visible effect, i feel like Ive done /something/ on her turn - where as visionary its PLay, Power draw with very little riders or effects or combos or chains)

 

I play Adept least, but thats mostly because I don't feel like dealing with the complexity he brings (same for AbZ)

 

Expatriette is my favorite - I play her far more than any other hero, with Fanatic a close second. Setback is enjoyable and the Sentinels are my favorite among the new heroes (though KNYFE is a close second)
